description: The YON domain for Lyt federated-vault storage. Defines the record families that Lyt vaults, meshes, and pods emit as their YON-as-source-of-truth. Ledger (@AUDIT / @PROVENANCE / @ROTATION) captures per-vault append-only audit, provenance, and month-rotation events. Mesh (@MESH / @MESH_HOME / @MESH_EDGE / @MESH_SUBSCRIPTION) declares a vault federation's identity — its push target, home vaults, edges, and subscriptions. Federation (@FEDERATION / @FED_MESH / @FED_AUTOMATOR / @FED_PRIMER / @FED_CANVAS) describes a pod's joined meshes, registered automators, and primer + canvas pointers. Lane (@LANE / @LANE_MEMBER) clusters figments by shared tag frequency into a per-vault search layer. Arc (@ARC / @ARC_MEMBER) orders figments into position-ordered narrative sequences. Vault-home-mesh (@VAULT_HOME_MESH) is a per-vault declaration of its owning mesh. Public-mesh (@MESH_PUBLIC / @UPDATE_CADENCE) carries publisher-declared discovery metadata and sync cadence for meshes advertised publicly.

records.description: Append-only audit log entry — every Lyt vault action that touches state (init, mesh-init, automator write, friction note, rebuild-index, …) emits one @AUDIT record to the vault's audit.yon ledger, followed by a chained @STAMP.

fields.name: ts
fields.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp the audited action took place

fields.name: actor
fields.description: Who performed the action — user:<handle>, automator:<name>/<ver>, agent:<name>, or system:lyt

fields.name: action
fields.description: Action verb — typically '<surface>.<verb>' (e.g. vault.init, mesh.add-edge, automator.write, friction.note, rebuild.ledger)

fields.name: target_type
fields.description: Kind of entity the action operated on — vault, mesh, edge, subscription, provenance, note, declaration, registry, etc.

fields.name: target_id
fields.description: Identifier of the targeted entity — rid string, vault-relative path, or natural-key identifier

fields.name: result
fields.description: Outcome of the action — defaults to 'success' when omitted

fields.name: details_json
fields.description: JSON-encoded extra context. Common keys: target_path, target_kind, run_id_hex, mesh_rid, fields_changed

records.description: Append-only provenance ledger entry — every automator-driven write emits one @PROVENANCE record carrying the full attribution chain (src + method + confidence + hash + tokens + cost + model + approver), followed by a chained @STAMP. Distinct from inline @STAMP records (which carry per-write provenance into note frontmatter / pre-declaration position): @PROVENANCE is the ledger-shape ARCHIVE; inline @STAMP is the per-write CARRIER. They coexist.

fields.name: target_type
fields.description: Kind of target the provenance attaches to

fields.name: target_id
fields.description: Identifier of the targeted entity — typically the vault-relative POSIX path for notes/declarations, or a rid for typed entities

fields.name: ts
fields.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp the write occurred

fields.name: src
fields.description: Who attribution — conventionally 'automator:<name>/v<ver>' (e.g. 'automator:metadata-filler/v0.1.0'); also accepts 'user:<handle>', 'system:lyt', 'agent:<name>'

fields.name: method
fields.description: Archetype-ish method label — filler, rollup, ingest, ai-relay, byok, etc.

fields.name: confidence
fields.description: Provenance confidence — 1.0 for deterministic writes, lower for LLM-attributed writes

fields.name: hash
fields.description: Content hash of the written payload — conventionally 'sha256:<hex>' (64 hex chars after the prefix)

fields.name: tokens
fields.description: Tokens consumed by an LLM call that produced this write (0 or omitted for deterministic writes)

fields.name: cost_usd
fields.description: USD cost of the LLM call that produced this write (0 or omitted for deterministic writes)

fields.name: model
fields.description: LLM model identifier that produced this write (omitted for deterministic writes)

fields.name: approver
fields.description: When the write required HIL approval (via @ESCALATE), the approver's rid is recorded here

fields.name: details_json
fields.description: JSON-encoded extra context (fields_changed, input_note_hash, mesh_context, etc.)

records.description: Month-boundary rotation event — `lyt housekeep` emits one @ROTATION record into the FRESH current-month ledger after renaming the prior file into the archive subdirectory. Followed by a chained @STAMP. The rotated archive is sealed; the new file opens with @DOC + @META key=month | value=<to_month> + @ROTATION + @STAMP.

fields.name: from_month
fields.description: Month-key of the archived file — YYYY-MM (UTC)

fields.name: to_month
fields.description: Month-key of the fresh current-month file — YYYY-MM (UTC); always > from_month

fields.name: archived_path
fields.description: Absolute filesystem path where the prior current-month file was renamed — conventionally <vault>/.lyt/ledgers/<name>/<from_month>.yon

records.description: Mesh declaration — a named group of vaults sharing a GitHub push target. Lives in the main vault's `.lyt/mesh.yon` as the source of truth for the mesh's identity, push target, and main vault binding. One record per mesh.

fields.name: rid
fields.description: Mesh rid — UUIDv7 in canonical 8-4-4-4-12 dashed form, prefixed mesh:

fields.name: name
fields.description: Mesh name — slug-safe segment (lowercase, [a-z0-9-]+, no Windows reserved names, no slashes; bare names, NOT owner/repo)

fields.name: push_target
fields.description: GitHub push target — handle or org name. Omitted when the mesh was created with `--no-push`.

fields.name: push_kind
fields.description: How push_target resolves — `handle` for personal GitHub accounts; `org` for GitHub organizations. Omitted under `--no-push`.

fields.name: main_vault_rid
fields.description: Rid of this mesh's main vault. Structurally invariant — the main vault is named `main` and cannot be renamed.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when the mesh was provisioned via `lyt mesh init`

fields.name: default_vault_update_cadence
fields.description: Mesh-level default sync cadence for home vaults that don't have their own @UPDATE_CADENCE record. Cron expression (5-field POSIX); applied per-vault as a fallback by subscribers' sync schedulers. Set via `lyt mesh update-cadence <mesh> --default-vault-cadence <spec>`. Omitted when no default is declared.

records.description: Mesh home-vault membership — one record per vault the mesh OWNS (vs references via @MESH_EDGE / @MESH_SUBSCRIPTION). The mesh's main vault always appears as a @MESH_HOME; additional homes accumulate as `lyt vault init <mesh>/<name>` lands non-main vaults.

fields.name: mesh_rid
fields.description: Rid of the mesh this home belongs to (matches the parent @MESH.rid)

fields.name: vault_rid
fields.description: Rid of the home vault

fields.name: vault_name
fields.description: Human-facing vault name — the leaf segment after the mesh/slash (e.g. main, journal, lyt). The main vault always has name=main.

records.description: Cross-mesh parent-child edge with rollup propagation — recorded in the REFERENCING mesh's mesh.yon (asymmetric awareness; the home mesh is unaware). Created by `lyt mesh add-edge --child <ref-vault> --parent <home-vault>`. Rollup propagates from child to parent.

fields.name: ref_mesh_rid
fields.description: Rid of the mesh recording this edge (the referencing mesh — the one whose mesh.yon contains this record)

fields.name: ref_vault_rid
fields.description: Rid of the home vault in ref_mesh_rid that acts as the PARENT in the parent-child relationship

fields.name: home_mesh_rid
fields.description: Rid of the mesh that owns the CHILD vault (the home mesh of the referenced vault — may be the same as ref_mesh_rid for intra-mesh edges)

fields.name: home_vault_rid
fields.description: Rid of the CHILD vault (the referenced vault, owned by home_mesh_rid)

fields.name: kind
fields.description: Edge kind — `parent` in v1; future kinds reserved

records.description: Flat cross-mesh reference — recorded in the SUBSCRIBING mesh's mesh.yon. The subscribed vault becomes searchable in the subscribing mesh's mesh-scoped queries but NO rollup propagates (compare @MESH_EDGE). Created by `lyt mesh subscribe --vault <ref-vault>`.

fields.name: mesh_rid
fields.description: Rid of the subscribing mesh (the one whose mesh.yon contains this record)

fields.name: external_vault_rid
fields.description: Rid of the subscribed vault (owned by external_mesh_rid)

fields.name: external_mesh_rid
fields.description: Rid of the mesh that owns the subscribed vault

fields.name: external_mesh_name
fields.description: Human-facing name of the external mesh — denormalized into the subscription record for fast list display without joining the registry

records.description: Publisher-declared discoverable metadata for a mesh advertised as a public mesh. Lives in the mesh's `.lyt/mesh.yon` alongside the @MESH header. Surfaced by `lyt mesh info` + `lyt mesh info --remote` (peek without cloning, via `gh api repos/{owner}/{mesh-main}/contents/.lyt/mesh.yon`). One record per mesh (the publish surface is a property of the mesh's identity). Absence = mesh is not publicly published; presence = publisher has run `lyt mesh publish`. Emitted in canonical key order for deterministic output.

fields.name: mesh_rid
fields.description: Rid of the mesh this public-metadata record belongs to (matches the parent @MESH.rid in the same mesh.yon)

fields.name: description
fields.description: Short human-readable description of the mesh — what knowledge it publishes, who it's for. Surfaced in `lyt mesh info`.
fields.example: Acme's open-source documentation and team handbook

fields.name: topics
fields.description: Comma-separated GitHub-style topic tags (publisher-declared; mirrors gh repo topics convention). Used for discovery filtering by `gh search repos --topic`.

fields.name: maintainer_contact
fields.description: Maintainer contact — typically an email address, but may be any contact URL (mailto:, https://, etc.). Used by subscribers reporting issues with the published content.

fields.name: maintainer_handle
fields.description: Maintainer GitHub handle (or org name) — denormalised display label for the mesh's primary maintainer. May differ from @MESH.push_target (e.g. handle is the human; push_target is the org).

fields.name: license_override
fields.description: SPDX-like license identifier overriding the LICENSE file at the main vault's root. Used when the mesh has a content license distinct from the repo license (e.g. CC-BY-4.0 for content; Apache-2.0 for the surrounding tooling). Omitted when the LICENSE file is canonical.

fields.name: accept_contributions
fields.description: Whether the publisher accepts external contributions via the standard OSS PR flow. Default semantics if omitted: true (contributions accepted on a best-effort basis). Explicit false signals a read-only publication posture.

fields.name: contribution_url
fields.description: URL to the publisher's contribution guidelines (typically CONTRIBUTING.md in the main vault repo). Required only when accept_contributions=true and contribution shape differs from standard OSS PR.

fields.name: homepage_url
fields.description: Publisher's main homepage URL — surfaced in `lyt mesh info`. Differs from the GitHub repo URL: homepage is the human-facing landing page.

fields.name: chat_url
fields.description: Publisher's primary chat/community channel URL — Discord, Slack, Matrix, IRC, etc. Used by subscribers seeking real-time help.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when the mesh was first published (when `lyt mesh publish` first ran). Distinct from @MESH.created_at (which records when the mesh itself was provisioned). Defaults to mesh-publish run time when omitted at first write.

records.description: Publisher-declared sync rhythm for a specific home vault in a public mesh. Lives in the mesh's `.lyt/mesh.yon`. Subscribers consume this record to drive their sync scheduler so they don't hammer GitHub polling. Zero-or-more records per mesh; sorted deterministically by vault_rid. Absence for a given vault = subscribers fall back to @MESH.default_vault_update_cadence (if set) or their local default. Cadence types: cron (POSIX 5-field), interval (seconds), on-demand (sync only when explicitly triggered).

fields.name: vault_rid
fields.description: Rid of the home vault this cadence applies to (matches a @MESH_HOME.vault_rid in the same mesh.yon)

fields.name: cadence_type
fields.description: How the cadence is expressed — `cron` requires the cron field; `interval` requires interval_seconds; `on-demand` requires neither (subscribers sync only on explicit trigger).

fields.name: cron
fields.description: POSIX 5-field cron expression (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week). Required when cadence_type=cron; omitted otherwise.

fields.name: interval_seconds
fields.description: Interval between syncs in seconds. Required when cadence_type=interval; omitted otherwise. Common values: 3600 (hourly), 86400 (daily), 604800 (weekly).

fields.name: timezone
fields.description: IANA timezone identifier (e.g. Europe/Bucharest, America/New_York, UTC) — applied when interpreting the cron expression. Defaults to UTC when omitted.

fields.name: peak_hours
fields.description: Comma-separated list of local-time hours (0-23) during which the publisher prefers subscribers to sync. Advisory only — subscribers may ignore. Empty / omitted = no restriction.

fields.name: on_demand_allowed
fields.description: Whether subscribers may force-sync outside the declared cadence window. Default semantics if omitted: true (subscribers free to override). Explicit false signals a strict cadence the publisher wants honored.

records.description: Per-vault home-mesh assignment — declares which mesh OWNS this vault. Emitted into the vault's own `.lyt/vault.yon` alongside the @VAULT record. Companion to @MESH_HOME (which is the mesh-side view of the same binding, living in the home mesh's `.lyt/mesh.yon`). Emitted when `lyt vault init`, `lyt vault clone --to-mesh`, or `lyt vault move` assigns a vault to a mesh.

fields.name: vault_rid
fields.description: Rid of this vault (matches the sibling @VAULT.rid in the same vault.yon file — round-trip self-reference)

fields.name: mesh_rid
fields.description: Rid of the mesh that owns this vault. Matches a @MESH.rid in some main vault's mesh.yon.

fields.name: mesh_name
fields.description: Human-facing mesh name — denormalised cache so a vault can name its home mesh without a registry lookup

fields.name: assigned_at
fields.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when the vault was assigned to (or moved into) the home mesh

records.description: Per-handler GitHub federation declaration — the source of truth for `{handle}/lyt-federation`, the per-user repo anchoring which meshes a handler participates in. Surfaced to handlers as 'Your Pod'. One record per federation; lives at `~/lyt/federation/{handle}/federation.yon`.

fields.name: rid
fields.description: Federation rid — UUIDv7 in hex (no dashes), prefixed fed:. Stable across rebuilds.

fields.name: handle
fields.description: GitHub handle that owns this federation repo. The federation repo full name is conventionally `{handle}/lyt-federation`.

fields.name: visibility
fields.description: GitHub repo visibility. Defaults to `private`; `public` is explicit opt-in.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when the federation was forged via `lyt federation init`

records.description: Per-federation joined-mesh record — one per mesh the handler participates in (own or join). Sorted deterministically by mesh_name (tiebreak by mesh_rid hex) in the emitted federation.yon.

fields.name: fed_rid
fields.description: Rid of the federation this mesh-membership belongs to (matches the parent @FEDERATION.rid)

fields.name: mesh_rid
fields.description: Rid of the joined mesh

fields.name: mesh_name
fields.description: Human-facing mesh name — denormalized for fast list display; primary sort key in deterministic output

fields.name: push_target
fields.description: GitHub push target for the mesh's main vault repo (handle or org name)

fields.name: push_kind
fields.description: How push_target resolves

fields.name: role
fields.description: Handler's relationship to this mesh — `own` if they hold push access to the mesh's main vault; `join` if they participate as a referencer/subscriber only

fields.name: added_at
fields.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when this mesh joined the federation

records.description: Per-federation automator registration — declares an automator visible across the handler's pod.

fields.name: fed_rid
fields.description: Rid of the federation owning this automator registration

fields.name: automator_rid
fields.description: Rid of the @AUTOMATOR record being registered (defined inline in a vault's `.lyt/automators/*.yon`)

fields.name: name
fields.description: Kebab-case automator name (matches the @AUTOMATOR.name field)

fields.name: version
fields.description: Semver version of the registered automator

fields.name: source
fields.description: Provenance category — `system` (first-party signed_by=system:lyt); `user` (handler-authored); `mesh` (mesh-published); `marketplace` (third-party distribution channel)

fields.name: enabled
fields.description: Whether the automator is currently active (default true)

fields.name: added_at
fields.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when the automator joined the federation

records.description: Per-federation primer document pointer — declares a federation-scope primer (the agent-priming markdown that orients a fresh agent session to the handler's pod).

fields.name: fed_rid
fields.description: Rid of the federation owning this primer reference

fields.name: primer_path
fields.description: POSIX path to the primer markdown relative to the federation-repo root

fields.name: scope
fields.description: Primer-coverage scope — `federation` is the cross-mesh handler-pod-wide variant; `mesh` is per-mesh; `vault` is per-vault

fields.name: cadence
fields.description: Regeneration cadence — cron string, ISO-8601 duration interval, `manual`, or `event:<trigger>`. Drives primer-generator scheduling.

fields.name: generated_at
fields.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of last primer generation

records.description: Per-federation canvas pointer — declares a federation-scope JSON Canvas document (cross-mesh visual map of the handler's pod).

fields.name: fed_rid
fields.description: Rid of the federation owning this canvas reference

fields.name: canvas_rid
fields.description: Rid of the canvas document — UUIDv7 prefixed canvas:

fields.name: title
fields.description: Human-facing canvas title shown in `lyt federation list --canvases` and similar surfaces

fields.name: canvas_path
fields.description: POSIX path to the .canvas file relative to the federation-repo root

fields.name: kind
fields.description: Canvas archetype — used for renderer hints + filter views; `custom` for handler-authored canvases

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when the canvas was first registered with the federation

records.description: Per-vault tag-frequency lane — a cluster of figments that share a source keyword (frontmatter tag). Emitted by `lyt vault rebuild-lanes` and by the lane-builder automator into `<vault>/.lyt/indexes/lanes.yon` (YON is the source of truth). Membership is materialised via companion @LANE_MEMBER records. Lanes use single-keyword-per-lane clustering (each tag with ≥threshold member notes becomes one @LANE with source_keywords=[tag]).

fields.name: rid
fields.description: Stable rid within a vault — `lane:<slugified-keyword>`. Slug = lowercase tag with non-alphanumeric runs replaced by `-`; e.g. `lane:software-design` for tag 'Software Design'.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Human-readable lane name — the original tag string verbatim (preserves casing + spacing for display).

fields.name: source_keywords
fields.description: Tags / keywords this lane clusters — emitted as a YON inline string-array (e.g. `source_keywords=["thinking","writing"]`). Single-element arrays (one lane per tag). Typed `string` at the schema level because the canonical type system enumerates only string|int|float|bool|ts atomics; composite shapes are described inline.

fields.name: mem_count
fields.description: Number of figments that belong to this lane. Equals the count of companion @LANE_MEMBER records.

fields.name: last_built
fields.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp the lane was last rebuilt — caller-controlled so test rebuilds round-trip byte-identically.

records.description: Membership row linking one figment to one @LANE — companion to @LANE. figment_rid is stored as a vault-relative POSIX path string. The companion cache schema in lyt.db uses TEXT for the figment_rid column accordingly.

fields.name: lane_rid
fields.description: Rid of the @LANE this membership belongs to.

fields.name: figment_rid
fields.description: Vault-relative POSIX path to the figment markdown file.

records.description: Per-vault position-ordered narrative arc — a sequence of figments that share a narrative thread (e.g. a writing series, a project thread, a thinking arc). Emitted by `lyt vault rebuild-arcs` and by the arc-builder automator into `<vault>/.lyt/indexes/arcs.yon` (YON is the source of truth). Membership is materialised via companion @ARC_MEMBER records whose `position:int` field carries 1-based ordering. Detection is two-source: (1) frontmatter `arcs: [name1, name2, ...]` arrays — each figment declares which arcs it belongs to; (2) manual @ARC + @ARC_MEMBER records embedded in figment markdown bodies — handler-authored records win over frontmatter-derived auto-assignment for the same (arc, figment) pair. Unlike @LANE (clustered by tag frequency), @ARC is always explicit — there is no threshold.

fields.name: rid
fields.description: Stable rid within a vault — `arc:<slugified-name>`. Slug = lowercase arc name with non-alphanumeric runs replaced by `-`; e.g. `arc:writing-the-paper` for name 'Writing the Paper'. Uses the same slugification as @LANE rids.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Human-readable arc name — preserves casing + spacing for display. Frontmatter-declared arcs use the verbatim string from the `arcs:` array; manual @ARC declarations override with their explicit name (handler-customised display label).

fields.name: category
fields.description: Arc category — handler-supplied label that groups arcs by kind (e.g. 'writing', 'thinking', 'project', 'series'). Defaults to 'uncategorized' when no manual @ARC declaration provides a category. Multiple manual declarations with conflicting categories resolve last-by-deterministic-file-path-order, emitting a warning rather than an error.

fields.name: last_touched
fields.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of the most-recently-modified member figment (max(mtime) across all members + any figment that declared the @ARC). Used by the primer-generator to surface recently-active arcs in cross-vault overviews.

records.description: Membership row linking one figment to one @ARC at a specific 1-based position — companion to @ARC. figment_rid is stored as a vault-relative POSIX path string. Position resolution: manual @ARC_MEMBER records pinned in figment markdown bodies reserve their explicit positions; frontmatter-derived members auto-assign positions starting at 1 in deterministic file-path order, skipping reserved slots. Position collision (two distinct figments claiming the same (arc, position) pair via manual records) is a fatal build error. The companion cache schema in lyt.db uses TEXT for the figment_rid column accordingly.

fields.name: arc_rid
fields.description: Rid of the @ARC this membership belongs to.

fields.name: figment_rid
fields.description: Vault-relative POSIX path to the figment markdown file.

fields.name: position
fields.description: 1-based ordinal position within the @ARC. Manual records carry explicit positions; frontmatter-derived members auto-assign in file-path order, skipping reserved-manual slots.

meta.tagline: Lyt storage architecture — per-vault append-only ledger family (audit, provenance, rotation) anchoring the YON-as-SoT contract

use_cases.title: Per-vault append-only audit trail
steps: Every Lyt verb that touches state routes through `recordAudit`
`recordAudit` appends an @AUDIT record + chained @STAMP to <vault>/.lyt/ledgers/audit.yon (atomic tmp+rename, fatal on YON failure)
Then INSERTs a row into <vault>/.lyt/indexes/audit.db (best-effort; rebuild-index reconstructs from YON on failure)
`lyt audit export` reads cache first, walks YON on cache-miss
use_cases.example: @AUDIT ts:ts=2026-05-30T14:30:00Z | actor="user:acme-handler" | action="vault.init" | target_type="vault" | target_id="personal-vault" | result="success"
use_cases.description: Markdown + YON are the source of truth, libSQL is a regenerable cache; the YON write is fatal-on-failure, the .db upsert is best-effort with a rebuild fallback.

use_cases.title: Automator-driven write provenance
steps: lyt-runner pre-write hook (`writeMarkdownWithStamp` / `writeYonWithStamp`) fires whenever an automator writes to a vault path under an active runContext
Markdown writes: `last_provenance:` frontmatter scalar upserted with the most-recent stamp
YON declaration writes: inline `@STAMP` record prepended before the new declaration
Hook appends a full @PROVENANCE record + chained @STAMP to <vault>/.lyt/ledgers/provenance.yon (fatal-on-failure)
Hook then INSERTs a row into <vault>/.lyt/indexes/provenance.db (best-effort)
Hook ALSO emits a companion @AUDIT record into audit.yon (action=automator.write, target_id=<provenance-id-hex>)
use_cases.example: @PROVENANCE target_type="note" | target_id="notes/2026-05-30-thought.md" | ts:ts=2026-05-30T14:30:00Z | src="automator:metadata-filler/v0.1.0" | method="filler" | confidence:float=1.0 | hash="sha256:abc…" | tokens:int=0 | cost_usd:float=0.0
use_cases.description: Six-step write contract: handler edits get an inert pass-through (runContext=null); automator writes get full provenance + audit emission.

use_cases.title: Month-boundary ledger rotation via `lyt housekeep`
steps: `lyt housekeep [--ledger <name>] [--rotate-now]` runs across every active vault × every known ledger
Reads `@META key=month | value=YYYY-MM` header (fallback: first @STAMP ts); compares to current UTC month
Creates fresh current-month file with header (@DOC + @META month) and emits one @ROTATION record + chained @STAMP
`--dry-run` reports proposed renames without mutating; `--json` emits deterministic output
use_cases.description: The rotation event lives in the FRESH file (not the archive) so the archive's terminal @STAMP closes a chain that the rotation marker doesn't perturb.

AUDIT.purpose: Per-vault append-only audit log entry — Lyt's compliance / SoC2-track ledger of every state-touching action. Records who did what to which entity, when, with optional structured details. The .db cache (audit_log table) is regenerable from YON.
AUDIT.when_to_use: Emitted by every Lyt verb that mutates state — directly via `recordAudit(vaultPath, db, args)` for handler-triggered actions, or indirectly via the lyt-runner pre-write hook for automator-triggered writes (which emits an @AUDIT companion alongside the @PROVENANCE).
related_standards: RFC 5424 syslog severity vocabulary (action verb conventions)

PROVENANCE.purpose: Per-vault append-only attribution ledger — the durable WHO-DID-WHAT-HOW record of every automator-driven write. Carries content hash, confidence, LLM token/cost/model metadata, and optional HIL approver. Distinct from inline @STAMP (which is the per-write CARRIER attached to the written artifact); @PROVENANCE is the ledger-shape ARCHIVE walked by `lyt provenance trace` and rebuild-index.
PROVENANCE.when_to_use: Emitted automatically by the lyt-runner pre-write hook (writeMarkdownWithStamp / writeYonWithStamp) when an automator writes under an active runContext. Handler-written notes (runContext=null) pass through with no @PROVENANCE emission — the ledger does not record every handler keystroke.

ROTATION.purpose: Month-boundary rotation marker — a one-line ledger event recording that the current-month file was archived and a fresh file opened. Lives in the FRESH file (after @DOC + @META month header), so the archive ledger's terminal @STAMP closes a complete chain at the boundary moment.
ROTATION.when_to_use: Emitted by `lyt housekeep` when a month boundary is detected OR `--rotate-now` forces rotation. NOT emitted on the no-op same-month path. Read by the `lyt vault rebuild-index --ledger <name>` walker to stitch archive + current files chronologically.
related_standards: logrotate(8) Unix conventions (archive naming + boundary semantics)
AWS S3 Glacier lifecycle transitions (boundary metadata)

ledger_header_convention.name: @LEDGER (a @DOC id-convention, not a separate tag)
ledger_header_convention.description: Every Lyt ledger file opens with a @DOC header whose id field encodes the ledger name + month. The @LEDGER 'tag' is implemented as this @DOC id-convention rather than a separate tag — it carries no fields of its own.
ledger_header_convention.rationale: Reusing core @DOC keeps the yai.lyt vocabulary smaller (convention over extension) and gets schema-level enforcement of the id slug shape for free via the core spec.

stamp_dual_role.description: Lyt uses core @STAMP in TWO distinct roles:

role_carrier_inline.name: Inline per-write provenance carrier
role_carrier_inline.where: Note frontmatter (`last_provenance:` scalar) AND pre-declaration position in YON files
role_carrier_inline.fields_used: ts, src, method, confidence, hash, tokens, cost_usd, model

role_chain_ledger.name: Per-record chain-hash carrier in ledger files
role_chain_ledger.where: Following every @AUDIT / @PROVENANCE / @ROTATION record in the ledger files
role_chain_ledger.fields_used: ts, src, hash (sha256 of prior file bytes; '-' for the first record)

stamp_dual_role.rationale: The INLINE per-write role is carried by @STAMP (the carrier role above). The ledger-shape @PROVENANCE record-type is a DIFFERENT shape — a per-ledger append archive. Both shapes coexist; @STAMP is reused for both chain-hash and inline carrier roles.

related_standards: YON-as-source-of-truth with a regenerable libSQL cache
POSIX rename(2) + NTFS MoveFileEx MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING (atomic file replacement)
RFC 9562 UUIDv7 (rid generation across Lyt + sibling tables)

@AUDIT records satisfy basic SOC2 audit-log requirements; audit-log governance overlaps with yai.compliance
